text:
tara-support: FYI customer ACME hit repeated 401s (invalid_api_key) after we rotated their key. They uploaded the new key into HashiVault via our onboarding script and then their service started failing. They pasted the vault config snippet and a cURL repro.
michael-eng: can you paste the raw export from Vault (redacted) and the curl you used? suspect encoding layer issue.
tara-support: paste from customer (redacted):
```
# curl to service (runs from their app box)
curl -H \"x-api-key: S0tFWT1FQkRPQ0tFQkRkRjIwMw==\" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
They said they used the dashboard key (visible as base64 string) and then stored it into Vault via `vault kv put secret/redwood key=@keyfile` (they uploaded file that already contained base64). Vault UI shows the secret value as `S0tFWT1FQkRPQ0tFQkRkRjIwMw==`.
liz-oncall: what's the API error payload? any server-side logs? deploy-bot: new error report attached -> `invalid_api_key` with header preview showing `x-api-key: 4b4b59=...` truncated.
michael-eng: hypothesis: the dashboard exports keys as base64-encoded bytes (that's how their key format is presented). Hashi Vault (or their sync process) has a transform plugin enabled that auto-decodes base64 on read, so when the app reads the secret it gets the decoded binary string, and then the client lib base64-encodes again (or vice-versa), ending up with an altered key. In short: double-encode/decode mismatch.
tara-support: customer says their runtime that reads vault is doing `base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(value)` in their app startup (they copied example from internal snippet). so yes, double decode very plausible.
michael-eng: repro steps I ran locally (short):
1) create a fake key bytes `echo -n \"my-secret-key-bytes\" | base64` -> `bXktc2VjcmV0LWtleS1ieXRlcw==`
2) store that base64 string into a file and `vault kv put secret/test key=@file`
3) read via `vault kv get -field=key secret/test` -> returns `bXktc2VjcmV0LWtleS1ieXRlcw==`
4) if client code does `decoded = base64.decode(value)`, the app sends `my-secret-key-bytes` (raw) to our API header; our service expects base64-encoded token and validates against stored base64 string -> 401.
michael-eng: quick curl repro I used (shows failing vs passing):
```
# failing (double-decode case)
curl -H "x-api-key: $(echo -n bXktc2VjcmV0LWtleS1ieXRlcw== | base64 --decode)" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# passing (send the base64 string we expect)
curl -H "x-api-key: bXktc2VjcmV0LWtleS1ieXRlcw==" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
liz-oncall: nice repro. what do we want to advise the customer? and is there anything we should change server side to surface clearer error? currently we return `invalid_api_key` with no hint about encoding.
tara-support: customer asked for immediate fix: they can either store the raw bytes in Vault (so their client doesn't decode) or disable the auto-transform on Vault (there's a transform policy flag `encoding=raw`). They want step-by-step to avoid downtime.
michael-eng: recommended message to customer (short):
- Confirm whether the value in Vault is base64 or already decoded bytes. In vault UI the alpha-numeric with `==` suffix indicates base64.
- If your app calls `base64.decode()` after reading secret, remove that call and pass the secret exactly as stored.
- Alternative: store raw bytes in Vault (upload the decoded file) and keep client decode step. Ensure one encode/decode only.
- Temp workaround: update startup to re-encode to base64 before sending: `encoded = base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString([]byte(value))` then use `x-api-key: encoded`. Not ideal but quick.
liz-oncall: I'll propose we update server-side error message to include an optional hint when format mismatch is detected: e.g. `invalid_api_key: possible-encoding-mismatch` (low-risk change) so support can triage faster. File a tiny follow-up RFC.
tara-support: customer confirmed they removed `base64.decode()` from their init and they are green now. will send the support reply and close after we draft the RFC.
michael-eng: put repro notes in internal doc and add unit test to server validation to detect obviously decoded tokens (eg non-base64 printable bytes) and return `possible-encoding-mismatch` with link to docs.
liz-oncall: filing P0->low PR: ENGR-1228: return encoding hint on 401 for obviously-mismatched token formats. tagging you @michael-eng. :+1:
tara-support: closing loop: told customer to rotate key via dashboard and re-seed Vault with the dashboard value (do not re-encode). they ack'ed. closing thread.
